items.name: Pañca Mahābhūta Śuddhi
items.one_line: Five element purification through movement, breath, and visualization
items.overview:
A complete body-mind preparation drawing on classical yoga's
five-element framework. Earth grounds. Water releases tension.
Fire ignites focus. Air balances prāṇa. Ether opens inner space.
Done before japa, the body becomes a steady, alert vessel for
hearing the Name.

steps.title: 1. Pṛthvī (Earth) — 2-3 min
steps.practice: Stand hip-width apart, eyes closed. Tilt forward (toes grip), back (heels press), left, right, return to center. Feel grounded — 'I am steady like a mountain.' Releases moha (scattered thoughts).

steps.title: 2. Jala (Water) — 4-5 min
steps.practice: Flowing movements: arm sweeps (6), side bends (6 each side), rope-pulling motions (12), gentle twists. Breath like waves (4 in, 6 out — longer exhale). Releases krodha (tension, anger).

steps.title: 3. Agni (Fire) — 3 min
steps.practice: Set intention: 'I release what does not serve me.' Bhastrikā with arm swings — sharp inhale (arms up), forceful exhale (arms down, fists). 3 rounds of 20-30. Releases kāma (lust, dullness).

steps.title: 4. Vāyu (Air) — 2-3 min
steps.practice: Nāḍī-śodhana (alternate nostril): close right nostril, exhale left (4), inhale left (4); close left, exhale right (4), inhale right (4). 3-5 rounds. Exhales longer than inhales. Releases lobha (imbalance).

steps.title: 5. Ākāśa (Ether) — 3 min
steps.practice: Cakra breathing: imagine breath rising from root to crown on inhale, descending on exhale. Three saṅkalpas: dhāraṇā ('I am present'), bhāva ('I chant to connect with Krishna'), bīja ('this mantra purifies my heart'). Releases mada (pride) and mātsarya (envy).

items.closing: Rub palms vigorously. Cup eyes with warm palms. Place palms on heart. Surrender the practice to the Supreme Lord. Begin japa immediately — do not delay.
items.source: Govardhana School of Yoga — Pañca Mahābhūta Śuddhi tradition

items.name: Samādhāya Mano Hṛdi
items.one_line: Bring the mind from the head to the heart, where Paramātmā resides
items.overview:
The master technique from SB 8.3.1 — Gajendra's formula. Krishna
sits in the heart as Paramātmā. To meet Him, bring the mind to
where He is. The head thinks, analyzes, doubts. The heart feels,
connects, trusts. Chanting from the heart transforms mechanical
japa into meeting.

steps.title: 1. Physical anchor
steps.practice: Sit comfortably. Place your hand on the heart center. Feel the physical heartbeat. This creates a body-mind connection.

steps.title: 2. Breath centering
steps.practice: Take 3 deep breaths. Exhale slowly, feeling the heart area. Each exhale releases mental tension. Let the shoulders drop.

steps.title: 3. Mental descent
steps.practice: Say mentally: 'Mind, we are going to the heart now.' Visualize consciousness moving from head to heart. Feel the shift from thinking to feeling.

steps.title: 4. Paramātmā awareness
steps.practice: Think: 'Krishna is HERE, in my heart.' Feel His presence — do not just think about Him. This is meeting Him where He resides. Sit with the awareness for one minute.

steps.title: 5. Maintain during japa
steps.practice: Chant with awareness in the heart, not the head. When the mind wanders into thoughts, gently bring it back to the heart. Each bead is a conscious calling, not a mechanical sound.

items.closing: After japa, place hand on heart again. Thank Krishna for the meeting. Carry the heart-centered awareness into the day.
items.source: HH Sacinandana Swami, 'Learning to Chant with Devotion'; rooted in SB 8.3.1 (samādhāya mano hṛdi)

items.name: Attentive Chanting
items.one_line: Train the ears to catch every syllable; let the calling mood arise
items.overview:
The core principle: we chant but do not HEAR. The Name speaks
through the mouth so the ear can receive it. Train the ear, and
chanting transforms from recitation into calling. Five techniques
that build attention round by round.

steps.title: 1. Syllable awareness
steps.practice: Hare Krishna mahā-mantra has 16 words and 32 syllables. Chant slowly enough to hear each one. Ask: can I hear all 32 syllables clearly? If not, slow down.

steps.title: 2. Speed calibration
steps.practice: Too fast → mind races ahead, doesn't hear. Too slow → mind wanders between words. Optimal: slow enough to hear each syllable, fast enough to maintain attention. Typically 6-8 minutes per round.

steps.title: 3. The calling mood
steps.practice: Transform chanting from recitation to prayer. Not 'Hare Krishna...' (mechanical) but 'Hare! Krishna!' (calling out). Chant as if calling a beloved child who is wandering away.

steps.title: 4. The listening posture
steps.practice: Sit where you can hear clearly (quiet space). Cup hand near ear if needed. Eyes closed or soft gaze down. Minimal movement. Position yourself as LISTENER, not just speaker. Ears primary, tongue secondary.

steps.title: 5. Emergency measures
steps.practice: Falling asleep → stand, walk, splash water. Racing thoughts → slow down dramatically. Emotional disturbance → pause, pray, then resume. Complete dryness → cry out sincerely for mercy.

items.closing: After japa, journal one word about today's hearing: 'attentive,' 'wandering,' 'dry,' 'sweet.' One word builds awareness over time.
items.source: HG Mahatma Prabhu's japa workshops and writings

items.name: The 4-Step Technique
items.one_line: Make a small doable request to the mind, then let mercy come
items.overview:
The signature method from HG Bhurijana Prabhu's VIHE Holy Name
Retreats and his book 'Japa: Nine Keys from the Śikṣāṣṭaka.'
Core principle: 'Let the mind embrace the Holy Name.' Not by
force but by patient repetition of a request the mind can accept.

steps.title: Step 1 — Saṅkalpa: 'Hear just ONE mantra'
steps.practice: Tell the mind a doable request it can comply with: 'Just hear this ONE Hare Krishna mahā-mantra completely.' If the mind is wild, ask for half a mantra. Hear every word with no distraction. Then: 'Just one more.' Then: 'Just one more.' Eventually the mind succumbs to the small request and becomes absorbed.

steps.title: Step 2 — Neglect the mind
steps.practice: As the mind becomes absorbed, it will periodically rebel and try to drift. Simply NEGLECT it. Like a child crying for something at a store — the stern parent ignores the misbehavior. The child eventually quiets. Do not engage with the wandering thought. Do not analyze why it came. Just return to chanting-hearing.

steps.title: Step 3 — Take shelter
steps.practice: The mind is now absorbed in the sound of the Name. Realize that the Holy Name IS Krishna Himself. Surrender completely. Accept Him in the form of the Name. Accept the Holy Name as everything and all that you really ever will need.

steps.title: Step 4 — Await mercy
steps.practice: If the Holy Name so desires, being pleased by your endeavor, He may bestow His mercy. A glimpse of real bhakti. A taste of His loving friendship. This step is not something you can force or demand. It is awaited, not manufactured. Received, not achieved. Be patient. Don't demand. Krishna reveals Himself when pleased.

items.closing: Hari Nāma ki jay! It really works. After japa, no analysis — simply gratitude for whatever was given. The mind that embraces the Name today is the mind that will embrace Krishna at the moment of death.
items.source: HG Bhurijana Prabhu, 'Japa: Nine Keys from the Śikṣāṣṭaka'; VIHE Holy Name Retreats
